prompt:
Production traces from the export service are being stitched together under the wrong request. The HTTP layer copies any X-Correlation-ID it is given, stores the active value through package-global state, and writes the response header too late. The asynchronous worker then consults that ambient state instead of the ID serialized on its job. Under overlap, one request's accepted log can disagree with its response and both jobs can acquire whichever ID was most recently seen. Values containing whitespace or delimiters can also reach logs and response metadata unchanged.

Repair correlation ownership at the transport boundaries without changing the exported handler, queue, worker, recorder, or source function shapes. A valid correlation ID is 8 through 64 ASCII characters, starts and ends with an ASCII letter or digit, and contains only ASCII letters, digits, `.`, `_`, or `-` in between. At HTTP ingress, accept the caller's value only when the header has exactly one value and that value is valid as-is. Missing, malformed, duplicated, or otherwise ambiguous headers must be replaced with one value from the injected Source. A generated candidate must pass the same validation before it is used; source errors, a nil source, or invalid generated candidates fail closed with HTTP 500, do not invoke the downstream handler, do not set X-Correlation-ID, and must not echo the rejected value. Set the resolved header early enough that it is present on every downstream response.

The queued Job must snapshot that resolved value. Job consumption is another transport boundary: preserve a valid serialized Job.CorrelationID, but replace a missing or invalid one through the worker's injected Source and update the Job value passed to the runner. If safe resolution fails, return the error without invoking the runner or recording job lifecycle entries. Otherwise the runner context plus `export.started` and `export.completed`/`export.failed` entries must all carry the same job ID. HTTP `export.accepted` logs, response headers, and enqueued jobs must likewise agree. Context values must remain stable after other requests are handled and under concurrent use; do not use mutable package globals. Preserve response status, account handling, source-error identity, lifecycle event names, failure identity, and the recorder/queue concurrency guarantees.

Run `go test -race -count=1 -timeout 30s ./...`. The acceptance test and go.mod are protected and must not be edited.

full_distill.primary_skill: establish validated correlation identity at HTTP and job transport boundaries, then propagate immutable operation-scoped values through responses, queued work, callbacks, and structured logs
full_distill.baseline_evidence: the race-enabled acceptance suite observes permissive hostile-ID validation, late response metadata, mutable context values, and workers correlating jobs from ambient request state instead of each serialized Job.CorrelationID
full_distill.success_contract: exactly one valid inbound token is preserved while every absent, hostile, or ambiguous value is replaced by a validated generated token; each operation retains one immutable ID across its response, job, callback, and logs, including concurrent requests and delayed workers
adversarial_factors: duplicate header fields include individually valid tokens, rejecting Header.Get-based first-value trust
generated values are independently validated and source failures retain error identity, rejecting the assumption that only clients are hostile
two queued jobs are processed after later requests and in reverse order, exposing workers that read ambient or most-recent request state
contexts are read again after other contexts are created and from synchronized concurrent goroutines, exposing mutable package globals even when sequential request tests appear correct
invalid queued IDs exercise the worker as a transport boundary and assert the normalized Job passed to the runner as well as both lifecycle logs
failure cases assert zero downstream calls and zero lifecycle logs, rejecting implementations that attach a safe-looking response ID after unsafe work already occurred
